object_description: two upper bodies set on freely arranged organic ground floor pavilions
geometry_property: two upper bodies placed on top
design_condition: the free organic pavilions at ground level follow the university logic while the two bodies above adopt the language and orientation of the polytechnic complex, forming a link between the two fabrics

positive: The project proceeds from a careful reading of the site and its construction over time
It tries to form a link between the two built fabrics
The intention is verified in the establishment of the built masses with great mastery
Organic ground floor volumes are established freely according to a characteristic pavilion logic
The two upper bodies adopt the language and main orientation of the neighbouring complex
The rigorous implementation and contextualised dimensioning are remarkable
The programmatic layout of the spaces linked to the different ground levels is remarkable
The western embankment height difference accommodates the auditorium
It is judiciously oriented towards the neighbouring campus via a low square
At the eastern end a high square responds with the cafeteria programme
The project is part of the site in good intelligence and without smug mimicry
It develops a critical, current and responsible point of view on the construction of the territory
Each floor is animated by a double-height meeting space, a welcome breathing space
At the base level removing the glazing suffices against overheating while keeping good daylight
negative: The radical separation gives both buildings an identical, excessively banal typology
The rooms align with a double central corridor surrounding blind service rooms
The breathing spaces are not enough to dispel the discomfort of endless corridors
The interior spaces lack the qualities expected of a place of study and exchange
The finesse of the territorial reflection finds no equivalent in the teaching and research space
There are no sanitary facilities in the cafeteria
Some technical rooms are understaffed and vertical circulation is undersized
The programme is resolved functionally but without great spatial qualities
The natural lighting of the floors is insufficient
The ventilated double skin facade is incomprehensible and prohibitive for the energy target
The double skin principle is anachronistic and useless though removable
The ground floor transition slab requires significant load absorption and large overhangs
Its minimised thickness probably requires prestressing
A very large excess floor area raises fears of a high construction cost
The cost of the work is well above the average of the completed projects
